newsitem.title: UK: Ivory Coast joins U.N. Common Fund for Commodities.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast joins U.N. Common Fund for Commodities.

text.p: Ivory Coast has joined the United Nations Common Fund for Commodities as the group's 104th member, the Amsterdam-based group said on Thursday.

The Fund was created under the U.N. Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) in 1980 to finance applied commodity research and projects such as collection of statistics and production information.
"It is expected that Cote d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast) will play an active role in the work of the Common Fund," a Fund written statement received here said.
The West African state is the world's top cocoa producer and a major coffee exporter.

The Fund said Ivorian Commodities Minister Alain Gauze would lead his country's delegation to the Fund's governing council meeting in Morocco in December. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
